key_insight: An independent certificate checker gives guaranteed error bounds for PDE solver outputs, including finite-element solutions and neural predictions, without trusting the solver.
engineering_relevance: Physics-based certificates can help validate automated simulation pipelines and learned surrogates when convergence alone misses incorrect solutions.
method: Return an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current alongside each prediction.
Use a small independent checker to bound error against the stated physics model.
Evaluate conventional solvers, deliberately buggy and LLM-written code, and neural surrogates.
evidence_signal: The checker rejected or refuted all five convergent buggy solvers and gave reduced-basis neural predictions certified intervals at most 0.0021% wide in-range and 0.3–25% wide out-of-range.
watch_item: Guarantees apply to the stated model, but bounds can be uninformative unless outputs are energy-accurate on a grid that resolves the problem.
paper_title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
